Q: Thank you for taking the time to speak with me today. This recorded statement concerns the collision you reported
in Sugar Land, Texas. Can you please state your full name for the record?
A: I'd rather not give my full name on a recording, but I can confirm I'm the driver of the vehicle involved.
Q: That's fine. Can you describe what happened as best you remember?
A: I was heading down the two-lane road in the early afternoon. A car coming the other way drifted into my lane and
we clipped each other nose to nose. It wasn't a big impact. Both of us were going slow, maybe fifteen or twenty miles
an hour.
Q: Did either vehicle leave the roadway or strike anything else?
A: No. We both stopped right there in the lane. Nothing else was hit.
Q: How did you feel immediately after the collision?
A: Honestly, I felt okay at first. I was a little shaken up, but I didn't think I was hurt. By that evening my neck was stiff
and I had a dull ache running into my shoulders.
Q: Have you sought medical treatment since the collision?
A: Yes, I went to urgent care the next morning. They diagnosed whiplash and told me to rest and take
anti-inflammatories. I've been doing physical therapy twice a week since then.
Q: Are you still experiencing symptoms?
A: Yes. Turning my head to the left is the hardest part, and I get headaches toward the end of the day. Sitting at my
desk for long stretches makes it worse.
Q: Is there anything else you'd like to add?
A: Only that I'm trying to keep working and do what my doctors ask. I'd appreciate any help with the medical bills.
Q: Thank you. I'll follow up with the documentation we discussed.
A: Thank you.
</page>

it is the loss date. Examples: "Date of loss:", "Crash date:", "Date of injury:", "the collision on".
